items.stem: What is meant by 'weathering' in the context of exogenic processes and weathering?
items.answer: The mechanical disintegration and chemical decomposition of rocks in place, through the action of weather and climate.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: weathering correctly explained as the mechanical disintegration and chemical decomposition of rocks in place, through the action of weather and climate.

items.stem: The following statement about mass movements, erosion and deposition is incorrect. Rewrite it correctly and justify your correction: "Creep is a rapid movement that can be seen easily."

items.stem: Which one of the following statements about endogenic processes: diastrophism and volcanism is correct?
items.answer: The earth's surface is shaped continuously by endogenic and exogenic forces.

items.stem: "Soil fertility increases with humus." Examine this statement with reference to soil formation and soil-forming factors.
items.answer: The statement is valid. Humus adds nutrients and improves the soil's capacity to hold water.

items.stem:
Statement: The surface of the earth is uneven.
Which one of the following best explains this statement?
items.answer: Endogenic forces build up parts of the surface while exogenic forces wear them down.
items.markingKey: (a) Endogenic forces build up parts of the surface while exogenic forces wear them down.
options: Endogenic forces build up parts of the surface while exogenic forces wear them down.
The heat generated within the earth and the thickness and nature of the crust are not uniform.
Large daily ranges of temperature cause rocks to expand and contract repeatedly.
Severe folding of long, narrow belts of the crust raises them into mountain ranges.

items.stem:
Read the following extract on mass movements, erosion and deposition and answer the questions that follow.
"Landslides are common in the Himalayas because of steep slopes, weak rocks and heavy rainfall. Deposition is the result of erosion, as the agents drop their load when their energy falls. Mass movements do not need a geomorphic agent such as water or wind."
(i) Mass movements take place mainly under the influence of: (1)
(ii) Explain the term 'mass movement' as it relates to this theme. (1)
(iii) Explain the reason behind the following: Landslides are frequent in the Himalayas. (1)
items.answer: (i) gravity (ii) The movement of rock debris down slopes under the direct influence of gravity. (iii) The slopes are steep, the rocks are young and weak, and rainfall is heavy.
items.markingKey: 1+1+1 marks: (i) gravity (ii) The movement of rock debris down slopes under the direct influence of gravity. (iii) The slopes are steep, the rocks are young and weak, and rainfall is heavy.
